title: Signature pad dark-mode contrast + crisp rendering; add falcon ID favicon assets; fix build/deploy asset issues

requirements.summary: Improve signature pad contrast in both light and dark themes by setting an explicit canvas background and theme-aware ink color.
acceptanceCriteria: In dark mode, the signature strokes are clearly visible while drawing (high contrast) without requiring users to change their OS/browser theme.
In light mode, the signature strokes remain clearly visible and the signature pad remains visually consistent with the rest of the UI.
The signature pad still supports mouse + touch drawing, clearing, and emits a PNG data URL via onSignatureChange when drawing ends.

file_operations.description: Update the signature pad to be theme-aware (e.g., via next-themes) and configure both: (1) an explicit canvas background fill color and (2) a high-contrast stroke (ink) color for light vs dark themes, while keeping existing mouse/touch handlers and PNG data URL emission on stroke end.

requirements.summary: Fix signature canvas sizing, DPR scaling, and clearing so strokes are crisp, coordinates align, and clear restores the intended background.
acceptanceCriteria: Signature strokes are crisp (not scaled/blurry) on standard and high-DPI screens.
Clicking “Clear” fully clears the signature content and restores the pad background so new strokes are immediately visible.
If the canvas is re-measured (e.g., initial render/layout changes), drawing coordinates still align with the pointer location.

file_operations.description: Implement robust canvas sizing that accounts for devicePixelRatio (set backing store size from CSS size, then set a non-compounding transform via setTransform), ensure coordinate mapping matches CSS pixels, add re-measure support (e.g., ResizeObserver or resize handler) to reinitialize the backing store safely, and update the Clear behavior to reset the surface including restoring the chosen background fill (not just clearRect).

requirements.summary: Add generated falcon “ID” favicon + apple touch icon assets and ensure they are served correctly from the existing HTML link tags.
acceptanceCriteria: The generated favicon file exists at frontend/public/assets/generated/falcon-ids-favicon-gothic.dim_32x32.webp.
The generated apple touch icon file exists at frontend/public/assets/generated/falcon-ids-apple-touch-gothic.dim_180x180.webp.
After building and deploying, browsers load the favicon and apple touch icon successfully (no 404s), and the icons visually depict a falcon with the letters “ID”.

file_operations.description: Add the generated WebP favicon asset at the exact required path so the existing frontend/index.html <link rel="icon"> reference resolves without 404s.
Add the generated WebP apple touch icon asset at the exact required path so the existing frontend/index.html <link rel="apple-touch-icon"> reference resolves without 404s.

Verify the existing favicon and apple-touch-icon <link> tags reference exactly /assets/generated/falcon-ids-favicon-gothic.dim_32x32.webp and /assets/generated/falcon-ids-apple-touch-gothic.dim_180x180.webp, and adjust only if necessary to ensure the deployed app loads the icons successfully.

requirements.summary: Audit and fix frontend build/deployment issues (missing assets and runtime errors) so production builds cleanly and key flows work without console errors.
acceptanceCriteria: A production frontend build completes without errors.
No missing static assets are referenced at runtime (no 404s for files referenced in HTML/CSS/TSX for critical UI paths).
Key user flows (sign-in, dashboard navigation, creating an order including signature capture) function without console errors in production mode.

file_operations.description: Harden signature pad initialization and cleanup to prevent production-mode runtime issues: ensure canvas context setup runs when the canvas is measurable, avoid transform compounding across re-measures, and ensure drawing/clearing logic cannot throw when the context is temporarily unavailable.
Audit and correct any missing/incorrect static asset references in the HTML head (especially icon paths/types) to prevent deployment-time 404s in production.

Confirm asset caching rules cover the favicon/apple-touch WebP assets and adjust match rules only if required to ensure they are shipped and cached appropriately during IC deployment (without changing unrelated security headers).
